findings.title: Known vulnerabilities in required development and build tooling
evidence: pip-audit reports pytest 8.4.2 affected by PYSEC-2026-1845 in both environments
pyproject.toml requires pytest>=8.3,<9, excluding patched pytest 9.0.3
pip-audit reports transformer setuptools 78.1.0 affected by PYSEC-2025-49 and PYSEC-2026-3447
QA-101 source constraints require pytest>=9.0.3,<10 and setuptools>=83,<84
both environments now use pytest 9.1.1 and setuptools 83.0.0 and pip-audit exits zero
the PostgreSQL-backed standard suite passes 291 tests with one expected skip and the transformer suite passes 292 tests
findings.impact: Fresh CI installs necessarily select a vulnerable pytest range, and transformer package operations use vulnerable build tooling.
findings.remediation: Validate pytest 9.0.3 compatibility, update source constraints, require setuptools>=83.0.0, rebuild both environments, and add dependency audit to CI.
findings.verification: Verified: both environment audits exit zero and both complete PostgreSQL-backed test suites pass.

findings.title: CI does not exercise the selected transformer path
evidence: CI installs only the Python 3.13 dev extra
the Python 3.12 transformer requirements are absent from CI
only the local transformer environment executes all 291 tests
QA-103 defines independent hash-locked standard and CPU-transformer Linux jobs with separate coverage outputs
the transformer job enforces offline Hugging Face operation, installs one isolated CPU Torch wheel, and explicitly deselects GPU acceptance
fresh Linux simulations pass 293 standard tests and 294 CPU-transformer tests using disposable PostgreSQL while governed data and artifacts are unavailable
GitHub Actions run 30161131645 passes both standard and transformer-cpu on commit 3c37677e08711697de6a89fde5b59231fef377b3
findings.impact: The selected model path can regress while required remote CI remains green.
findings.remediation: Add a bounded Python 3.12 CPU transformer CI job and explicitly separate GPU-only acceptance tests.
findings.verification: Verified: GitHub Actions run 30161131645 passes both jobs and the transformer job produces its separate coverage report.

findings.title: Fresh-environment dependencies are not fully locked
evidence: standard dependencies are version ranges without a lock file or hashes
tokenizer requirements use exact versions without hashes
the CUDA torch hash is a comment rather than an enforced require-hashes install
QA-102 adds five reviewed platform-specific lock artifacts with enforced SHA-256 hashes
clean Python 3.13 standard and Python 3.12 transformer environments installed only the reviewed third-party locks plus no-dependency editable Git source
both clean environments passed pip check and their complete PostgreSQL-backed suites
the CUDA index is isolated to one no-dependency torch 2.13.0+cu130 wheel with its official SHA-256 digest enforced
findings.impact: Future environments may resolve different transitive packages than the accepted validation environment.
findings.remediation: Generate reviewed standard and transformer lock files with hashes and deterministic rebuild/update instructions.
findings.verification: Verified: clean hashed standard and transformer installs pass pip check and both complete PostgreSQL-backed suites; exact lock digests and package-source boundaries are repository-tested.

findings.title: Coverage gaps are measured but not enforced
evidence: full transformer branch coverage is 71 percent
model_selection.py is 49 percent, transformer_fit.py 41 percent, transformer_training.py 35 percent, and abstention_analysis.py 63 percent
CI defines no coverage fail-under threshold
findings.impact: Critical orchestration and error branches can lose coverage without failing CI.
findings.remediation: Add focused failure-path tests and a non-decreasing branch-coverage ratchet for both environments.
findings.verification: Both CI jobs meet explicit coverage floors and protected modules increase from the audited baseline.

findings.title: Alembic cannot detect model-to-migration drift
evidence: alembic check reports that env.py supplies no SQLAlchemy MetaData
the sole head and database current revision both remain 0004_temporal_split
disposable migration integration tests pass
findings.impact: A future schema-model change can omit a migration without an automated drift warning.
findings.remediation: Define authoritative SQLAlchemy metadata in the migration environment and add alembic check to CI.
findings.verification: alembic check and disposable upgrade tests pass from a clean checkout.

findings.title: The public repository main branch is unprotected
evidence: GitHub branch API reports main_protected=false
origin/main matches the audited commit
the latest CI run for the audited commit succeeded
QA-104 GitHub API verification reports strict required standard and transformer-cpu contexts
pull-request delivery, administrator enforcement, linear history, and conversation resolution are enabled
force pushes and branch deletion are disabled
findings.impact: Evidence and governance controls can be changed through direct or destructive pushes without a review gate.
findings.remediation: Protect main, require CI, and block force pushes and branch deletion.
findings.verification: Verified: the GitHub branch API reports the accepted protection controls and both required job contexts for main.

findings.title: Security checks are manual and not merge gates
evidence: manual current and historical high-confidence secret scans found zero matches
CI has no secret, dependency, SBOM, or container scan
no automated dependency update configuration exists
GitHub Actions are referenced by major tags rather than immutable commits
findings.impact: Credential, dependency, image, or workflow supply-chain regressions may merge undetected.
findings.remediation: Add redacted secret scanning, pip-audit, SBOM and image gates, automated dependency updates, and immutable Action pins.
findings.verification: Clean scans pass and controlled secret/vulnerability fixtures fail without exposing matched values.

findings.title: No static type-checking gate exists
evidence: no mypy, Pyright, or equivalent configuration is tracked
CI runs linting and tests but no type checker
production modules expose annotated protocols and typed boundaries that are not statically verified
findings.impact: Interface and nullable/dynamic errors remain dependent on runtime path coverage.
findings.remediation: Adopt one checker incrementally, establish a clean scoped baseline, and ratchet the protected module set.
findings.verification: The configured checker passes locally and in required CI for its declared scope.

findings.title: Critical orchestration is concentrated in large functions
evidence: cli.py is 598 lines and main is approximately 375 lines
transformer_fit.py is 1103 lines and contains a function of approximately 209 lines
transformer_calibration.py is 1013 lines and contains a function of approximately 205 lines
findings.impact: Review, isolated testing, and safe changes to orchestration and error paths are unnecessarily difficult.
findings.remediation: After adding characterization tests, extract command handlers and pure validation and report-building functions.
findings.verification: Public interfaces and generated reports remain unchanged while complexity and function sizes decrease.

findings.title: Retention deletion is governed but operationally manual
evidence: ADR 0009 requires local deletion by 2026-11-19 end of day Asia/Singapore
the tested cleanup command and deletion evidence format exist
no scheduled reminder or automated deadline preflight is tracked
findings.impact: Maintainer omission could retain sensitive source narratives beyond the approved local period.
findings.remediation: Add a local-only deadline guard and runbook checkpoint without uploading or backing up the data.
findings.verification: Time-bound tests prove reminders and expiry rejection, and cleanup emits aggregate-only deletion evidence.

findings.title: Trusted-local artifacts use executable serialization
evidence: the baseline path uses joblib.load after path, size, and SHA-256 verification
transformer resume uses torch.load with weights_only=false after path, size, identity, and SHA-256 verification
the artifacts are ignored, local-only, and not accepted from a service or upload
findings.impact: Integrity hashes do not authenticate an artifact if a local attacker can replace both the artifact and its manifest.
findings.remediation: Document the trusted-local-only boundary and prefer non-executable or restricted serialization where practical.
findings.verification: Untrusted or out-of-bound artifact paths are rejected and the accepted serialization policy is tested.

findings.title: Test runs emit dependency deprecation warnings
evidence: the standard full suite emitted five joblib and NumPy deprecation warnings
the transformer full suite emitted the same five warnings
findings.impact: Warning noise can hide future actionable warnings and foreshadow dependency incompatibility.
findings.remediation: Identify and resolve the originating dependency path, then establish a warning budget.
findings.verification: Both full suites run without unexpected warnings.

findings.title: Standard public-repository security metadata is incomplete
evidence: no SECURITY.md is tracked
no standalone LICENSE or CODEOWNERS file is tracked
pyproject.toml explicitly states All rights reserved
findings.impact: External vulnerability reporting, ownership, paper-artifact reuse, and permissions are less clear to reviewers.
findings.remediation: Add a security policy and ownership metadata and make an explicit licensing decision for code and paper artifacts.
findings.verification: Repository metadata links correctly and states reporting, ownership, and reuse terms unambiguously.
